title: Commitment Cadence & Fallback Lane Strategy — Q3 Plan for Reserved GPU Pools
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Objective: Define and deliver a quarterly plan that coordinates reserved GPU commitment cadence with a set of deterministic fallback lanes (aka burst lanes) to preserve customer SLAs when demand spikes or forecasting misses. This initiative focuses on three deliverables for Q3: 1) commitment cadence playbook that prescribes commit window sizes and roll-forward rules for customers on Dedicated; 2) implementation spec for fallback lanes (policy + pricing) that automatically route overflow to burst capacity with latency and cost guardrails; 3) a set of experiments and dashboards to measure economics and SLO impact before full rollout.

Background: We have recurring customer requests for predictable throughput during launches and marketing spikes while keeping unit economics reasonable. Current autoscale behavior is reactive and opaque to customers; reserved pools sometimes under- or over-commit relative to actual usage patterns. We will introduce more explicit cadence windows for reservation commitments and pair them with fallback lanes to reduce customer-visible failures and to limit surprise billing.

Scope: Roadmap and implementation spec for Dedicated offering and Console UX changes to expose commit cadence and fallback lane controls. Includes orchestration rules, pricing band recommendations, observability requirements, and rollout playbook. Excludes on-prem package changes and major billing system rewrites (out of scope for Q3).

Success criteria (high level): Stabilize P50 latency for committed customers during spikes, reduce emergency on-call pages tied to capacity overrun by 60%, and demonstrate <10% delta in unit cost for typical burst scenarios against baseline after fallback lanes are enabled.
acceptance_criteria: Commitment cadence playbook published in Confluence including windows, renewal rules, and customer-facing wording
Fallback lane policy spec (routing + pricing + throttles) reviewed by eng and finance
Console UX mockups for commit cadence and fallback lane toggles approved by Design
End-to-end canary that routes 5% of traffic through fallback lanes with metrics and rollback criteria
Dashboards tracking cost per token, P50/P95 latency, 429/503 rate for committed customers during spikes
milestones: 2026-03-20: Playbook draft complete and stakeholder review
2026-04-10: Tech spec and SLOs approved by Eng and SRE
2026-04-24: UX prototypes validated with 3 pilot customers
2026-05-15: Canary rollout to 5% traffic with monitoring
2026-06-30: Q3 launch (soft) with monitoring and cost guardrails
decisions: Use a two-tier fallback lane model: 'warm burst' (pre-warmed reserved nodes with time-limited extra capacity) and 'elastic surge' (pay-as-you-go scaled GPUs with higher price multiplier)
Charge fallback lane by effective token-hours with a transparent multiplier disclosed in Console
Enforce a 10-minute cooldown window for automated scale-down from fallback lanes to avoid flapping
Canary will run in us-west-2 region first, then eu-west-1 if metrics are stable
risks: Forecast misses could still exhaust fallback lanes if multiple large launches coincide
Pricing multiplier risks reducing customer adoption unless communicated clearly
Technical: orchestrator latency when routing to fallback lanes could add tail latency if KV cache miss amplification occurs
Billing integration delays could block visibility into cost impacts for customers
